documents.unit: Technology & Innovation / Vice President for Academic Affairs
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: Davidson College IT policy on AI covering community-wide privacy and recording rules, data classification and approved platforms, academic uses, and administrative procurement. For teaching it delegates decisions to individual faculty, strongly urges syllabus statements, and treats violations as Honor Council matters. It is reviewed every six months (last March 2026).
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Faculty individually set the policy for acceptable use of AI in their classes, if any, on a course-by-course and/or assignment-by-assignment basis", so the college sets no stance itself and delegates to instructors; it offers no tiers.

units.why: The Background says "The exploration of AI capabilities is essential to meet the college’s mission of preparing its students for lives of leadership and service", an institution-level preamble on why engaging with AI matters; P56 (preamble stating purpose and principles), not a skills rule.
units.anchor: The exploration of AI capabilities is essential to meet the college’s mission
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 with actor admin; B coded P44 (professional-skill rationale) with actor all. The source ties AI exploration to the college mission of leadership and service, not to employer-expected skills, so P44 does not fit and P56 follows. Actor all because the preamble addresses the whole community; unit stance encourage because exploration is called "essential".

units.why: Background states that AI presents "ethical, professional and legal issues" and that guidance is needed for appropriate use; it frames the policy purpose and scope, so P56 (institution-wide framework).
units.anchor: guidance is required to ensure the college meets its obligation to use AI
units.frag_start: At the same time, guidance is
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. The sentence "guidance is required to ensure the college meets its obligation to use AI in appropriate ways" is a real statement of why the policy exists; kept as P56.

units.why: The Background lists "generative AI (genAI), retrieval augmented generation, agentic AI systems, and similar capabilities", which fixes what the policy covers, so it is a definition of scope (P61).
units.anchor: including generative AI (genAI), retrieval augmented generation, agentic AI systems, and similar capabilities
units.frag_end: teaching, learning, research and administrative use.

units.why: The Purpose says the policy is "to detail the current acceptable practices for use of AI at Davidson", an institution-wide statement of purpose and scope (P56).
units.anchor: to detail the current acceptable practices for use of AI at Davidson
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. The purpose sentence sets "acceptable practices for use of AI at Davidson" for the whole community, so all. Type P56 agreed.

units.why: Community members "should consult their dean, vice president or division head" when the policy does not address a question. This is the ask-first rule for unsure cases (P10), not a delegation of the stance.
units.anchor: should consult their dean, vice president or division head for guidance
units.frag_end: acceptable uses of AI if this policy does not address them.

units.why: AI wearables and transcription tools "must be used in ways that balance productivity and convenience with a respect for all participants' privacy". It is a privacy rule on a class of AI tools (P50), not a course-level stance.
units.anchor: balance productivity and convenience with a respect for all participants’ privacy

units.why: "Must receive affirmative permission of all participants" before recording or summarizing a conversation with a wearable is a consent requirement protecting personal data (P50).
units.anchor: must receive affirmative permission of all participants before using the technology
units.frag_start: Individuals wishing to use a recording

units.why: Points to the Academic Regulations policy on recording classes, which sets terms for recording teaching activity; a cross-reference on class recording privacy, P50.
units.anchor: sets forth the terms and conditions for recording a class or other organized teaching activity
units.frag_start: The Audio and Visual Recording of Classes policy
units.policy: The Audio and Visual Recording of Classes policy in the Academic Regulations sets forth the terms and conditions for recording a class or other organized teaching activity.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. The sentence says the Academic Regulations recording policy "sets forth the terms and conditions for recording a class"; it is a real cross-reference to a recording rule, kept as informs under P50.

units.why: The Code of Responsibility "Invasion of Privacy" section sets expectations on recordings; a cross-reference to existing rules on recordings, P50.
units.anchor: sets forth expectations regarding audio, video and other recordings
units.policy: The Invasion of Privacy section of the Code of Responsibility in the Student Handbook sets forth expectations regarding audio, video and other recordings.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. The sentence says the Code of Responsibility "sets forth expectations regarding audio, video and other recordings"; a real cross-reference to a recording rule, kept as informs under P50.

units.why: When a platform records or transcribes, it "must provide a conspicuous notice to all participants". This is a notification duty on AI transcription for privacy (P50).
units.anchor: the platform must provide a conspicuous notice to all participants of the feature’s use
units.frag_start: If a collaboration platform is enabled
units.resolution_why: B merged this sentence and the next into one unit (actor all); A split them. The source states two rules ("the platform must provide a conspicuous notice" and "the meeting host must disable"), and one unit per rule is required, so we follow A. Actor admin for the platform notice duty.

units.why: "The meeting host must disable" recording and transcription on request of any participant, a privacy safeguard for AI transcription in Davidson-licensed services (P50).
units.anchor: the meeting host must disable the use of recording and transcription capabilities
units.resolution_why: Found only by A as a separate unit (B merged it into the notice unit). It is a distinct rule: "Upon request from any participant, the meeting host must disable the use of recording and transcription". Hosts can be anyone, so actor all rather than A's instructor.

units.why: Transcripts of meetings and classes "should by default be considered private" and not shared without permission of all participants. This is data protection for AI-generated records (P50).
units.anchor: should by default be considered private among those who participated
units.frag_start: Recordings and transcripts of meetings, classes

units.why: "Public data may be uploaded to or analyzed in any publicly-available AI platform" permits one data class on any tool; it is part of the data-handling rules that govern tool choice (P50).
units.anchor: Public data may be uploaded to or analyzed in any publicly-available AI platform

units.why: "Internal and Restricted data may only be uploaded to or analyzed in a college-provided AI platform" requires vetted institutional tools for sensitive data (P50).
units.anchor: may only be uploaded to or analyzed in a college-provided AI platform

units.why: The text lists "the provided platforms" (Amplify, Google Gemini, ChatGPT Pro and Claude Pro licenses) maintained by T&I; this is provision of sanctioned institutional tools, P17. Informs because it states a fact about what is provided.
units.anchor: Amplify (pro-level ChatGPT and Claude) - amplify.davidson.edu
units.policy: The provided platforms are Amplify (pro-level ChatGPT and Claude), Google Gemini, and college-provided ChatGPT Pro and Claude Pro licenses.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P17, informs, all, general. They differed on unit stance (A permit, B encourage). The text only lists what is provided and does not recommend using it, so permit.

units.why: "Confidential data may not be uploaded to or analyzed in any AI platform without review" by the Information Security Program Manager; a prohibition protecting confidential data (P50).
units.anchor: Confidential data may not be uploaded to or analyzed in any AI platform without review

units.why: "Individual employees and departments should not license their own AI tools without approval from T&I" steers people to vetted, centrally purchased tools (P50); it is not a vendor-contract review rule (P65).
units.anchor: should not license their own AI tools without approval from T&I
units.frag_start: Individual employees and departments should not
units.resolution_why: Phase differed: A before-course, B general. The sentence on employees and departments not licensing their own AI tools without T&I approval is a standing community rule, not tied to course set-up, so general. Type P50, actor all, modality should-not agreed.

units.why: Faculty AI use in teaching is "subject to professional standards and guidelines" from the VPAA, faculty governance and societies; instructor-use rule, P59.
units.anchor: subject to professional standards and guidelines issued by the Vice President for Academic Affairs
units.frag_start: Faculty use of AI tools in
units.policy: Faculty use of AI tools in their teaching, research and creative work is subject to professional standards and guidelines issued by the Vice President for Academic Affairs, faculty governance, and professional societies.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded must. "is subject to professional standards and guidelines" binds faculty AI use to external standards, so it is a duty (must), not a mere fact. Type P59, actor instructor and phase general agreed.

units.why: "Faculty individually set the policy for acceptable use of AI in their classes... course-by-course and/or assignment-by-assignment" is the delegation of the stance to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: Faculty individually set the policy for acceptable use of AI in their classes

units.why: "Students should consult the course syllabus and the instructor for guidance on permissible uses of AI" tells students where to find and confirm the rule; it fits the ask/check-first type (P10) better than P04 because it addresses students.
units.anchor: Students should consult the course syllabus and the instructor for guidance

units.why: "Davidson may provide AI tools accessible to all students to ensure equitable access" gives an equity rationale for providing tools. I chose P51 (equity and access) over P17 because the stated aim is equal access, though the tools themselves are listed under P17 elsewhere.
units.anchor: Davidson may provide AI tools accessible to all students to ensure equitable access
units.resolution_why: Phase differed: A general, B before-course. The sentence says what the institution may provide, an institutional set-up decision, so before-course. Type P51 and actor admin agreed.

units.why: "The availability of an AI tool from the college does not correspond to permission to use the capabilities of that tool in a particular course" says the course rule still controls. P04 (per-course decision) fits; P11 is about carry-over between courses.
units.anchor: does not correspond to permission to use the capabilities of that tool
units.frag_start: The availability of an AI tool from the college
units.resolution_why: A coded P04 (during-work, restrict); B coded P11 (course-start, neutral). P11 covers permissions that do not carry from one course to another; this sentence says a college-provided tool's availability is not permission in a particular course, so the course rule decides, which is P04. Phase during-work because it concerns when students use the tool; unit stance restrict because availability is not permission.

units.why: "Faculty are strongly urged to include a generative AI statement on their syllabi" recommends a syllabus statement, which is P09; "strongly urged" makes it should rather than must.
units.anchor: Faculty are strongly urged to include a generative AI statement on their syllabi
units.resolution_why: Unit stance differed: A neutral, B encourage. "strongly urged" recommends the statement, so encourage (modality should). Type P09 agreed.

units.why: "Resources are available to support faculty in developing these statements" points faculty to support for writing syllabus statements (P63).
units.anchor: Resources are available to support faculty in developing these statements
units.resolution_why: A coded actor instructor and B admin. The text says "Resources are available to support faculty in developing these statements", a support offer addressed to faculty; actor instructor. Type P63 agreed.

units.why: "Violations of this policy may be handled as with any matter of academic integrity, including... referral to the Honor Council" classifies misuse as an integrity matter (P36). "May" is permissive, so modality is may.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy may be handled as with any matter of academic integrity
units.frag_start: Violations of this policy may be handled
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, unit stance neutral; B coded all, restrict. The text says violations "may be handled as with any matter of academic integrity ... Honor Council", describing a college process rather than a position on AI use, so admin and neutral. Type P36 agreed.

units.why: Departments wishing to procure AI solutions "must review the request with T&I" and contracts must be approved by the CIO; vendor review rule, P65.
units.anchor: must review the request with T&I
units.frag_start: any college department or division wishing to procure
units.policy: Any college department or division wishing to procure a technology solution that provides or uses AI capabilities must review the request with T&I.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P65, admin, before-course, must. B restricted the unit stance; A neutral. The passage is an internal review procedure, not a restriction on AI use, so neutral. The anchor alone lacks its subject, so a normalized policy is given for the first rule only; the contract-approval clause in the same sentence is not merged in.

units.why: "College agreements for the use of AI should include language governing the privacy and security of Davidson's information, as well as how the solution provider may use Davidson data to train" models: limits on vendor use of institutional data (P65).
units.anchor: should include language governing the privacy and security of Davidson’s information
units.frag_start: College agreements for the use of AI should
units.resolution_why: Both coded P65, admin, before-course, should. Unit stance differed (A neutral, B restrict). Requiring agreements to include language on privacy and security is a contracting procedure, not a limit on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: Departments using AI to do staff work "should review their planned uses with the CHRO and CIO" before starting; an administrative-use rule about workforce impact that fits no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: should review their planned uses with the Chief Human Resources Officer
units.frag_start: Departments and divisions intending to use AI
units.uncovered_note: Review of AI uses that would perform or displace work ordinarily done by college staff, with CHRO and CIO review.
units.resolution_why: Both coded UNCOVERED, admin, before-course, should; unit stance differed (A neutral, B restrict). It is a workforce-impact review procedure, not a limit on AI use, so neutral. No existing type covers review of AI uses that replace staff work, so UNCOVERED stands.

units.why: Where AI "would displace existing college staff", the CHRO and CIO prepare a recommendation for the President. It is a distinct escalation step on workforce displacement, with no matching type.
units.anchor: the CHRO and CIO will prepare a recommendation of the proposal
units.frag_start: For use cases where such AI technology would displace
units.uncovered_note: Escalation of AI proposals that would displace staff: CHRO and CIO recommendation to the President.
units.resolution_why: Modality differed: A must, B informs. "the CHRO and CIO will prepare a recommendation" assigns a duty to named officers, so must. UNCOVERED agreed: no type covers escalation of staff-displacing AI proposals.

units.why: AI-generated public-facing content "is governed by communications guidelines" from College Communications; a rule for AI-made materials but not course materials, so not P48; UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: is governed by communications guidelines promulgated by College Communications
units.frag_start: The use of AI to generate public-facing content
units.policy: The use of AI to generate public-facing content such as websites, audio or video content, or other materials for public dissemination is governed by communications guidelines promulgated by College Communications.
units.uncovered_note: AI-generated public-facing marketing and communications content is governed by College Communications guidelines.
units.resolution_why: Both coded UNCOVERED, all, general, informs. B gave a normalized policy, which is faithful and used because the anchor alone omits what is governed. No type covers administrative rules for AI-made public-facing content (P48 is course materials).

units.why: Users "are cautioned that the copyright implications of works created in whole or in part using AI technology are uncertain": a copyright and ownership caution (P52).
units.anchor: copyright implications of works created in whole or in part using AI technology are uncertain
units.frag_start: Additionally, users of generative AI tools are cautioned

units.why: Creators of works the college may claim copyright in "are advised to seek advice on the current state of AI and copyright before using AI": advice on copyright of AI output (P52).
units.anchor: are advised to seek advice on the current state of AI and copyright
units.frag_end: before using AI in their work.

units.why: Points to US Copyright Office resources as helpful guidance on AI and copyright, P52.
units.anchor: One helpful source of guidance is the U.S. Copyright Office
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. "One helpful source of guidance is the U.S. Copyright Office’s resources on copyright and AI" recommends a resource on AI and copyright; a real, if minor, pointer, kept as informs under P52.

units.why: "The Chief Information Officer is responsible for ensuring that this policy is reviewed every six months": a fixed review cycle (P54).
units.anchor: responsible for ensuring that this policy is reviewed every six months
units.frag_start: The Chief Information Officer is responsible

units.why: Assigns ownership: the VPAA with faculty bodies for academic AI policy and the senior leadership team for administrative and community-wide policy; governance, P56 (P54 is the review cycle).
units.anchor: is responsible for college policies on academic uses of AI
units.frag_start: The Vice President of Academic Affairs (VPAA), with input
units.policy: The VPAA, with input from faculty governing bodies, is responsible for college policies on academic uses of AI; the senior leadership team is responsible for concurring on policies governing administrative and community-wide uses of AI.
units.resolution_why: Phase differed: A general, B over-time. The sentence assigns ownership of the policy framework (who is responsible for academic and administrative policies), not a review step, so general; P56 agreed (P54 is the review cycle in the previous unit). B's normalized policy is used because the anchor omits the senior leadership team clause. Phase set to general.

notes: Single college-wide IT policy (last reviewed March 2026); no school or computing policy found; course layer deferred. The first privacy sentence is duplicated in the source and coded once. Starter topic code governance is used for administrative and framework units because the starter list has no closer code.
